meanings.note: Singular only. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'honesty' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The main thing in a person is honesty.

examples.text: У Самсонова есть главное — честность и порядочность. Все говорят, а он делает!
examples.trans: Samsonov has the main thing — honesty and decency. Everyone talks, while he gets things done!

meanings.note: The т is not pronounced: [чесный]. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('honest').

examples.text: Я ухожу. Ваш сын будет бедным и честным.
examples.trans: I'm leaving. Your son will be poor and honest.

meanings.note: Often with a hint of 'bureaucrat'. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'official, bureaucrat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.
